recognize_zh: 骨小樑邊緣呈不規則扇貝狀（scalloped），小樑之間的骨髓腔被鬆散的纖維組織與梭形細胞取代，幾乎看不到造血細胞，符合腎性骨病變的纖維性骨炎（osteitis fibrosa）。
features: Thick, irregular bone trabeculae with scalloped, eroded margins suggesting increased resorption
Intertrabecular marrow space replaced by loose fibrous stroma with scattered spindle-shaped fibroblast-like cells
Paratrabecular accentuation of cellular fibrous tissue along bone surfaces
Scattered small osteocyte lacunae within eosinophilic lamellar/woven bone
Near-absence of recognizable hematopoietic elements and fat cells in this field
describe_en: Bone marrow trephine biopsy (H&E, faded older preparation) shows thickened, irregular bone trabeculae with scalloped resorptive margins. The intertrabecular spaces are occupied by loose fibrous tissue containing scattered spindle cells, with paratrabecular accentuation, and normal hematopoietic tissue and fat are essentially absent in this field. Discrete osteoclasts and osteoid seams cannot be reliably assessed at this magnification and staining quality. In the setting of untreated chronic renal failure, findings are consistent with osteitis fibrosa (renal osteodystrophy due to secondary hyperparathyroidism) with marrow fibrosis contributing to anemia.

ddx.vs: PMF shows reticulin/collagen fibrosis with clustered atypical megakaryocytes and osteosclerosis, whereas renal osteodystrophy shows peritrabecular fibrosis with scalloped resorption and osteoclast activity without megakaryocytic atypia.
The marrow and bone changes are morphologically identical; distinction depends on renal function and serum calcium/phosphate/PTH profile.
Metastases show cohesive epithelial clusters within the fibrosis (keratin positive), which are not seen in this image.
Paget disease shows a mosaic pattern of irregular cement lines and large multinucleated osteoclasts rather than predominantly peritrabecular fibrosis.
